notes: Event date: 28 March 1945, noon (Stacey, p. 539). Event definition: At noon the corps takes the 3rd Canadian Division and its sector of the bridgehead east of the Rhine under command; the 3rd Division had fought under the 30th Corps since the crossing, and the 2nd Division crosses the Rhine on 28-29 March. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 539: "At noon that day the 2nd Canadian Corps (still under the Second Army) took the 3rd Canadian Division, and its sector of the bridgehead, under command"; p. 541: "The 2nd Canadian Division, which had been resting in the Reichswald, crossed the Rhine on 28-29 March". current_activity: Returns to First Canadian Army at 23:59 on 1 April from Second Army; the drive north begins from Emmerich
notes: Event date: 1 April 1945, 23:59, one minute before midnight of 1-2 April (Stacey, p. 545). Event definition: The corps operations east of the Rhine pass from Second Army to First Canadian Army at one minute before midnight of 1-2 April; the 4th Armoured Division moves into the bridgehead on 1 April, and Crerar issues a new directive to his corps commanders on 2 April for the corps advance to the north. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 545: "At one minute before midnight of 1-2 April Headquarters First Canadian Army took control of the 2nd Canadian Corps' operations east of the Rhine"; p. 546: "General Crerar issued a new directive to his Corps Commanders on 2 April"; "The 4th Canadian Armoured Division moved in here on 1 April". G. Simonds (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 30 Jan. 44 to 25 Jun. 45).

current_activity: Crossing of the Ijssel between Zutphen and Deventer by the 1st Canadian Division, temporarily under the corps
notes: Event date: 11 April 1945 (Stacey, pp. 551 and 569). Event definition: On 11 April the 1st Canadian Division, temporarily under the corps, launches the assault across the Ijssel midway between Zutphen and Deventer, the first operation of that division in north-west Europe. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 569: "it was not until 11 April that the 1st Division, temporarily under the 2nd Corps, was able to launch this attack"; p. 551: "was launched by the 2nd Infantry Brigade on the afternoon of the 11th, about midway between Zutphen and Deventer". Location: Zutphen, Gelderland with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: the point is Zutphen, one of the two towns that bound the crossing front; it is not a headquarters position. Location support: Stacey places the crossing midway between Zutphen and Deventer (p. 551). Commander: Lt.-Gen. G. G. Simonds (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 30 Jan. 44 to 25 Jun. 45).

composing_text: CAN-ARM-005D (5th Canadian Armoured Division, passed under the corps on 21 April)
current_activity: 5th Armoured Division joins the corps; divisional tasks for the final operations assigned at a conference on 20 April
notes: Event date: 21 April 1945 (Stacey, p. 591). Event definition: The 5th Canadian Armoured Division passes under the corps on 21 April while moving from western Holland, after the corps commander assigns tasks to his divisions on 20 April. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Simonds (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 30 Jan. 44 to 25 Jun. 45).

composing_text: UK-INF-003D (3rd British Infantry Division, with the corps from 28 April to 6 May)
current_activity: Employs four Canadian divisions, the 1st Polish Armoured Division and, from 28 April to 6 May, the 3rd British Division
notes: Event date: 28 April 1945 (Stacey, p. 591). Event definition: For the final operations in the Emden-Wilhelmshaven peninsula and towards Oldenburg the corps employs the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Canadian Divisions, the 1st Polish Armoured Division and, from 28 April to 6 May, the 3rd British Infantry Division. Location: Oldenburg, Niedersachsen (existing place PL0657) with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: the point is Oldenburg, the main objective of the corps in these operations; the corps headquarters place is not stated. Location support: Stacey names Oldenburg and the Emden-Wilhelmshaven peninsula as the corps objectives (pp. 591 and 598-603). Commander: Lt.-Gen. G. G. Simonds (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 30 Jan. 44 to 25 Jun. 45).

current_activity: Meeting at Bad Zwischenahn on the details of the German surrender in the corps sector; about 30,000 Germans reported
notes: Event date: 5 May 1945 (Stacey, p. 613). Event definition: A meeting to implement the surrender is held in the burgomaster office at Bad Zwischenahn; General Straube, commanding Armeeabteilung Straube, reports to General Simonds that there are about 30,000 German troops in the sector. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 613: "On the 2nd Canadian Corps front a meeting to implement details of the surrender was held in the burgomaster's office at Bad Zwischenahn on 5 May"; "reported to General Simonds that there were approximately 30,000 German troops in this sector". Location: Bad Zwischenahn, Niedersachsen with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the meeting place, not the corps headquarters, which Stacey does not name. Location support: Stacey names the burgomaster office at Bad Zwischenahn as the meeting place (p. 613). Commander: Lt.-Gen. G. G. Simonds (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 30 Jan. 44 to 25 Jun. 45).
